parts.name: Bell
parts.info: The outer can that spins. It carries the magnets on its inside wall and turns the shaft; on a drone the propeller is mounted on top of it.

parts.name: Magnets
parts.info: Permanent magnets glued around the inside of the bell, alternating north and south. The stator's changing field pulls them round. This model has 10; real FPV motors typically have 14 (approx.).

parts.name: Shaft
parts.info: Steel shaft fixed to the bell, running through the two bearings in the stator.

parts.name: Windings
parts.info: Copper coils around the stator teeth, in three phases. The ESC switches current through them in turn, which makes a rotating magnetic field.

parts.name: Stator core
parts.info: Laminated iron teeth that carry the coils and guide their magnetic field toward the magnets (approx.: identified from the shape).

parts.name: Base
parts.info: The fixed base that holds the stator and the bearing tube; it bolts to the frame (approx.).

parts.name: Base pins
parts.info: Eight small pins or screws in the base (approx.: identified from the shape).

parts.name: Upper bearing
parts.info: Ball bearing: inner and outer race, a ring of balls and a cage keeping them apart. It lets the shaft spin with little friction.

parts.name: Lower bearing
parts.info: The second ball bearing, at the bottom of the bearing tube.

parts.name: Retaining screw
parts.info: Holds the shaft in the bearings from below (approx.).

parts.name: Phase leads
parts.info: Three wires, one per phase, from the windings to the ESC. Swapping any two reverses the direction of rotation.

parts.name: Lead sleeve
parts.info: Sleeve where the leads leave the motor (approx.).

parts.name: Bullet connectors
parts.info: Gold-plated bullet plugs on the ends of the leads, for connecting to the ESC.
